state:
Milestone `dossier`, goal `the-description-is-owed`, stage 2. `data/proofs/policy.json` carries
`owes.all.about: true`, and every feature whose examples are on disk has its description: the 13
sections of `tools:config` were the last, and `bun nv proofs --verify --group tools:config` passes.
`bun nv proofs --gate` names 13 of 1159 features: the 5 of `tools:install` and 8 of `tools:server`,
which owe a test, an example and an attack beside the description, and five of them a code sample in
their reference section.

**The run is held for the user: the chain order cannot reach this goal.** Its last check is the
whole roster, and goals `tools-install` and `tools-server` own those 13 features and sit behind
this goal in `data/chain.json`. This goal writes a description from examples already on disk
(`docs/agent/goals/the-description-is-owed.md` § *The item list*), and those features have none.
Only the driver moves `live`, and `bun nv chain --move` edits `goals` alone. The repair is the
user's: set `live` to the goal that should run now and move `the-description-is-owed` behind
`tools-server`. Nothing else is open under this goal.

**Two things for the user to look at.** `docs/reference/tools/20-config.md:65-70` says `nvs run`
enforces `[limits] memory` alone and that the server, database client and logger are not in the
binary. Line 165 of the same chapter says `memory` and `cpu_time`, a run under `cpu_time = "1s"`
stops with `FATAL: the request exceeded its CPU-time limit`, and `nvs --help` lists `serve`. The
paragraph was left as it stands, because rewriting it needs each block checked against `nvs run`,
and the new descriptions state none of it. Carried forward and not re-checked: gap
`nvs-ir/throws-on-an-array-key-that` was moved from owner goal `coalesce-assign` back to
`milestone: M10`, and `docs/agent/goals/coalesce-assign.md` still has that goal delete it.

The pack does not print `docs/examples/README.md` § *The description*; it is one `bun nv peek`.
A group is checked with `bun nv proofs --gate --group '<G>'`.
